free_tier.stated: No free tier: the Cold Archive class is billed from the first GiB at USD 0.0000027 per GiB-hour (about USD 0.001971 per GiB-month), with no capacity cap stated; a 180-day minimum storage duration is billed and data retrieval costs USD 0.01062 per GiB
free_tier.notes: billed per GiB-hour; the monthly figure is the hourly price x 730 hours

per_object_cap.stated: 48 TiB per object through multipart upload (up to 10,000 parts of 5 MiB to 5 GiB); 5 GiB through a single PUT
per_object_cap.notes: the Object Storage technical limits page states one set of limits for the Object Storage offer

retention.stated: no expiry stated; a minimum storage duration of 4,380 hours (180 days) is billed per object, and an object deleted or moved to another class earlier is charged for the remaining hours
retention.notes: a billing minimum, not a deletion clock

egress.terms: External ingoing and outgoing traffic free and API requests free; an object is read back only after a restore request, which carries the per-GiB retrieval fee and bills the restored copy upfront at the Standard Multi Zone rate of USD 0.00002152 per GiB-hour for the number of days set in the request
egress.price_per_tb: USD 9.89 per TB retrieved, the retrieval fee; outgoing traffic itself is free

interface_detail: S3-compatible API, reachable only from the Paris 3-AZ region (EU-WEST-PAR)
tooling: AWS CLI, rclone, any S3 SDK; lifecycle rules supported
chaining: archive tier behind a hot S3 bucket: lifecycle rules move objects from Standard or Infrequent Access into Cold Archive, and a restore brings an object back into the Standard class for reading

limits.value: 48 TiB per object by multipart upload; 5 GiB by a single PUT

limits_note: Restore time: from a few minutes to several hours for a few megabytes up to a terabyte, and at most 48 hours for hundreds of terabytes; data sits on magnetic tape; a 180-day minimum storage duration is billed per object
